narrative: The model estimated that your chance of becoming a bad credit risk was 41.0%. The lending decision uses a strict approval cut-off, so that estimated risk was considered too high, and your application was denied. The strongest influence was your credit history, which in this case counted in your favor rather than against you; it was the top-ranked factor, even though your file is recorded as critical/other credits. The next most important factor was your checking account status: having a balance of 0–200 DM pushed the decision toward bad credit, and this status is much less common among approved applicants, most of whom have no checking account balance recorded. Your savings below 100 DM was the third most important factor and also pushed toward bad credit. Together, these two risk signals outweighed the favorable credit-history signal. You should ask the lender for a full explanation and whether an appeal or manual review is possible. To strengthen a future application, focus on building savings, avoiding a low checking balance, and reducing the requested amount or term. Providing updated income information or a guarantor may also help; reapply only when your financial profile is stronger.
